documentation: The front-end enforcement manifest (docs/FRONTEND.md, Modules).
This file began as the epic's grandfather record and is no longer one. Both
allowlists it carried are gone: fstring_documents emptied in issue 241 and
module_isolation_exemptions in issue 234, and the closeout (issue 245) deleted
the empty lists along with the code that read them, because a list with nothing
on it is still a place to add something. tests/test_frontend_ratchets.py and
tests/js/module-isolation.test.mjs now reject the first violation of either rule
outright.
What remains is permanent, not debt, and still only moves one way (AGENTS.md).
inline_script_ceilings: exact permitted count of inline-script source
lines per Jinja template (docs/FRONTEND.md, Modules: templates carry no
logic in <script>). The metric is defined in tests/test_frontend_ratchets.py
and is enforced as an equality, so moving glue into a module fails the
check until the ceiling is lowered in the same pull request. A template
absent from this map must carry no inline script. Every scripted page now
sits at 1 -- the single entry invocation the rule permits beside the bundled
text -- which is the floor, not a number still coming down. The 404 is
recorded at 0, because shipping no script at all is a decision there
(docs/FRONTEND.md, Modules) rather than an absence nobody reached yet.
module_injection_placeholders: the `{{ name | safe }}` lines each template
may use inside a <script> element to inline a module. Placeholder lines are
excluded from the line count, so an unregistered one would be an unmeasured
way to inject Python-built script; registering them makes an added
injection point a checked change. `inside a <script> element` is meant
literally, and includes the payload element the ceiling above skips: `|
safe` writes its value unescaped, so a placeholder there could close the
payload and open an executable element. The lines of a payload are outside
the ceiling; a placeholder alone on its line inside one is not outside the
registry.
The scan reads Jinja's own forms: `{{- x | safe -}}` whitespace control and a
dotted `{{ obj.attr | safe }}` are registered, and the registered name is the
whole expression, so `guide.entry` and `entry` are different entries. The
element matcher tolerates `</script >` and `</script\n>` for the same reason.
Both were gaps issue 250 found and issue 245 closed, each with a case that
fails when its pattern is reverted.
One residual limit is recorded rather than closed, because closing it would
change the registry's unit from the line to the occurrence: the registry
matches only a line that is nothing but a placeholder. A `| safe` sharing its
line with other content is counted by the ceiling inside an ordinary <script>
-- the safe direction -- but inside a payload element, whose lines the ceiling
skips, it is read by neither half. No template writes that form; a reviewer
adding one to a payload element is what this note is for.
Placeholders outside every <script> -- the stylesheet each page inlines --
are not covered here. The shell's head links, band, and footer stopped
being placeholders in issue 241: they are macros in
rendering/templates/_shell.html.j2 now.
